text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.
LONDON - The UK's FTSE 100 index finished higher for the eighth consecutive session on Thursday boosted by sharp gains in banking stocks and a firm start in New York.
But traders said gains were capped in the run-up to next Thurday's election and volume remained slim at 699 million.
The leading index ended just 0.8 points firmer at 4,388.5 after earlier touching 4,400.4.
FRANKFURT - German shares ended largely flat in bourse trade on Wednesday as a rise in the DAX futures market provided some insulation from overnight losses on Wall Street.

The DAX-30 index of leading German shares closed 1.41 points up at 3,397.36, with June DAX futures reversing late Wednesday losses to trade 31 points up at 3,401.0. In post-bourse trade the DAX was up 29.62 at 3,369.49.

PARIS - French shares closed with a small gain on Thursday after a rumour, later confirmed, of an opinion poll giving the centre-right a small majority after the election. The market had been on the look-out for opinion polls, having had only a quick CSA poll of Tuesday which saw the ruling coalition maintaining a majority, albeit reduced. The CAC-4- rose 6.19 points to 2539.83.

ZURICH - Swiss shares again finished at a record close on Thursday after the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) touched 4,836.1 points during the session on average volume. The positive interest rate environment, a somewhat firmer dollar, technical factors and options-related trading supported the market.
The SMI finished up 1.15 percent or 55 points at 4,836.1. The all-share Swiss Performance Index added 0.93 percent or 28.26 points to finish at 3,051.18.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed slightly lower as profit-taking emerged near the end of the session to erase gains brought on by a pension fund shopping spree. The buying at one point lifted the Nikkei 225 average near the 19,000 barrier, but it ended down 37.40 points or 0.20 percent at 18,698.07.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks rallied in the final minutes of trade on Thursday to close slightly higher on buying in laggard blue chips and with sentiment again fired by enthusiasm for mainland companies.

The Hang Seng Index closed 19.79 points, or 0.16 percent, higher at 12,726.83 after trading in negative territory for most of the day. Turnover was a heavy HK$13.51 billion, higher than Wednesday's HK$9.90 billion.
SYDNEY - Australian shares finished slightly firmer in quiet trade ahead of the ANZAC Day long weekend with local investors reluctant to take positions ahead of two Wall Street sessions.
Australian markets will be closed on Friday for ANZAC Day.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed up 2.4 points at 2,474.7, after touching an intra-day high of 2,480.2.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial shares ended slightly firmer, riding up on the back of an early rise on Wall Street and retracing the losses seen during most of an active day's trade, dealers said "The industrials are closing on the up side, obviously the Dow has something to do with that. The Dow is up very, very strong," one dealer said.
The industrial index ended up 10.6 points to finish at 8,425.4, the gold index shed 1.3 points to close at 1,230.5 and the all-share index gained 7.7 points to 7,087.9.
